surface_mechanism_description: Ligand exchange between TMA and surface hydroxyl groups followed by water pulse to regenerate OH sites.
evidence: The preparation of oxide layers by molecular layering is based on self-restrained chemisorption of metal halide (MCl n) and water vapor under the conditions close to monolayer surface coverage. For instance, on a hydroxylated surface of silicon, this process can be described by the following chain of surface reactions: Si–OH) + MCl n (Si–O–) MCl n + HCl, (2) Multiple repetition of reactions (1) and (2) with the intermediate removal of excess reagents and reaction products results in the formation of an oxide layer of the required thickness.
